title: Dashboard trim & escalation runway for token paths (working notes)
content:
Context:
This doc collects rough decisions for a short runway to: (1) trim expensive dashboard panels tied to tokenized inference (esp. KV-cache/TTL heavy panels), and (2) define the SLO escalation path + tracing anchors we want attached to each dashboard lane so oncall can act quickly without digging through 10 different traces.

Goals (what success looks like):
- Reduce average dashboard query cost for the inference workspace by ~35% during heavy traffic while preserving operator investigability.
- Define a 3-step escalation path for latency/throughput regressions in token-serving paths with concrete playbook actions.
- Provide a minimal set of trace-anchor templates and span tags to attach to new panels and probes.

Principles (quick):
- Keep investigation-first panels, but move high-cardinality sampling to a separate "deep-dive" view behind a low-cost gate.
- Prefer synthetic microprobes + lightweight session slices to expensive ad-hoc SQL queries.
- SLO alerts should point to a single playbook link and an annotated trace anchor example.

Metric definitions (compact):
- token_latency_p50_ms, token_latency_p95_ms, token_latency_p99_ms: time from request received by routing -> first byte produced (ms). Exclude queued time if >5s (that's a separate queue metric).
- kv_cache_hit_rate_percent (per-tenant, per-model): hits / (hits + misses) over 5m. Use approximate cardinality if tenant count > 2000.
- prefix_warmth_index: fraction of requests with cache warmness >= 0.8 on first n=3 tokens. (heuristic for cold-start investigations).
- model_fanout_factor: number of model-shards engaged per request (avg over 1m). Important for quantizing backend cost.
- effective_token_cost_usd: token_count * per_token_unit_cost (rollup), used for cost anomalies.

Panels we should prune / move (proposal):
- "All-tenant top 100 kv miss queries" -> move to deep-dive deck and replace with sampled "kv miss headcount" and heatmap with 1/10th sampling.
- Raw per-token user prompt text panel (redacts) -> remove from default dashboard; keep in audit-only panels with access controls.
- Full-span flamegraphs for every rollout -> keep only for nightly builds; on alert generate ad-hoc.

Tracing anchors and recommended span tags (templates):
- Anchor: request.session_id -> include as span attribute 'rw.session_id' (obfuscated if PII).
- Anchor: routing.decider -> span name: routing:select-model, tags: {rw.route_reason, rw.model_variant, rw.customer_tier}.
- Anchor: runtime.kv_cache -> span names: kv.check and kv.prefetch. Tags: {rw.kv_key_hint, rw.kv_hit: true|false, rw.cache_ttl_s}.
- Anchor: execution.tokenize -> span name: model.tokenize; tags: {rw.token_count, rw.truncation_policy}.
Notes: prefer boolean tag names for quick filters (rw.kv_hit:true). Use numeric tags sparingly for cardinality.

Escalation runway (3-step) - for token latency SLO breaches:
1) Auto triage (0-5 min): run synthetic microprobe and compare kv_cache_hit_rate_percent + prefix_warmth_index to baseline. If kv hit drops >10%: add incident label kv-cold. Slack: #oncall-observability ping.
   - Action: toggle fast fallback routing for affected customers (if enabled).
   - Owner: oncall.
2) Investigate (5-30 min): open single annotated dashboard view for tenant cohort. Pull the top 3 traces using trace anchor: routing.select-model -> runtime.kv_cache -> model.exec.
   - Action: identify fanout spikes or model-variant slow nodes; if model-side, route to Dedicated fallback.
   - Owner: oncall + eng-serving-runtime on-call (pager binds).
3) Remediate (30+ min): if root cause is infra (OOM, eviction storms), escalate to SRE playbook and enact scale/burst policy. If internal regression, roll back model or rollout.
   - Action: trigger rollback/A-B fallback and run admission-control on future deploys.
   - Owner: SRE + release eng.

Dashboard trimming checklist (practical):
- For every expensive panel (queries > 2 CPU-min/day): annotate owner and move to deep-dive or add explicit sampling param.
- Add a low-cost summary tile per team that links to the deep-dive; the summary should be <=3 KPIs.
- Replace high-cardinality group_by with approximate sketches or top-k + long tail bin. Document approximation semantics in tooltip.
- Add a "cost estimate" badge to each panel (simple monthly $).

Experiment log (notes):
- 2025-11-12: A/B moved kv miss query to sampled heatmap -> query cost -28%, operator feedback: slightly slower for rare tenants.
- 2025-12-01: Added prefix_warmth_index -> helped reduce false positives in synthetic probes.

Open questions / tradeoffs:
- Sampling: target 1/10 for row-level queries, but critical tenants need full fidelity. How to mark a tenant as critical? Proposal: tag in tenant metadata + dashboard filter.
- Trace retention: 7d full traces and 30d sampled. Ops asked for 14d. Cost tradeoff analysis pending (OBS-482).

Immediate next actions (owner -> due):
- Avery: produce trimmed-dashboard PR with cost-badges + move list (due 2026-01-20) -> linked OBS-482.
- Marcus: add trace example snippets for runtime.kv_cache and push to observability repo (due 2026-01-18).
- Priya: run cost simulation for 7d vs 14d trace retention and add to confluence (due 2026-01-25).

Notes-to-self / rough ideas:
- Consider a toggle that flips a panel between "operator" and "developer" modes with different sampling and retention.
- Could auto-generate playbook links from alert rule metadata (embed JIRA ids).
- Short term: prefer actionability > completeness. Keep the most useful panels and ship simple playbook anchors.

References and quick links:
- OBS ticket: https://redwood.atlassian.net/browse/OBS-482
- PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/observability/pull/278
- Confluence draft: confluence:Observability-Dashboard-Guide-2025

End of notes.

(If you copy anything here into a formal doc, please run it by release eng + SRE for rollout gating.)
